contrast_correction.what_was_wrong: A table-header contrast defect was PRESENT in the original 22 September build and survived the restoration, because the restoration deliberately reproduced the previous render byte-for-byte and therefore also reproduced the defect. In header cell 3 of the v0.5 gate table on page 15 (the table headed 'Gate | Passes when | Does not pass'), the word 'not' rendered in house navy (21,35,60) on the house navy header fill (21,35,60) - a contrast ratio of 1.00, i.e. invisible. Cause: the markdown header row is '| Gate | Passes when | Does **not** pass |', so the renderer emits not inside the ; the stylesheet rule 'strong { color:#15233c; }' then set the text navy while the header fill stayed navy.
contrast_correction.what_it_was_NOT: The defect was NOT the one described in the briefing. It was reported that the unscoped rule 'tr:nth-child(even) td { background:#faf8f3; }' was overriding the header background, turning header cells after the first one pale under paper-coloured text (white-on-pale). That was tested directly and does not occur in this paper, for two independent reasons, both verified with headless Chrome. First, the selector's subject is 'td', and the renderer emits header cells as 'th', so the rule cannot match a header cell at all. Second, no table in this paper has an even-numbered header row: all 15 tables have exactly one <tr> inside <thead>, and it is nth-child(1) of thead in every case, so 'tr:nth-child(even) th' matches 0 elements. Measurement of the restored render found 0 white-on-pale spans and 53 of 53 header bands on the house navy. The white-on-pale rule was nevertheless applied as asked, because it is correct defensive styling.
contrast_correction.what_was_changed: In _build_v05\build_v05.py only. No markdown was touched. Three edits: (1) the header rule scoped from 'th' to the house pattern 'table thead th'; (2) the zebra rule scoped from 'tr:nth-child(even) td' to 'table tbody tr:nth-child(even) td' and given an explicit colour, so it can never reach a header; (3) a new rule 'table thead th strong, table thead th em, table thead th code { color:#f7f4ee; }' added, which is what actually removes the page-15 defect. The pale zebra band was NOT darkened and the striping was NOT removed - 215 pale body-row bands still paint.
contrast_correction.standing_check_added: _build_v05\build_v05.py now runs check_contrast() as the last step of the page check and exits non-zero on any finding. It detects, on every rendered page: text that is white or near-white on a pale background; any dark table-header band whose fill is not the house navy; and any span below the WCAG AA contrast ratio for its size (so a dark-on-dark pair cannot hide by being neither of the first two). Verified against the unfixed render, where it failed with 1 finding (page 15, ratio 1.00, 'not').
